The main takeaway from our work is that

the toxicity of complex petroleum substances, like the ones that are spilled in the environment, can be predicted by using a model that accounts for the physical-chemical properties of the individual hydrocarbons that make up the complex mixture, as well as the partitioning between oil droplets and dissolved phases.

the toxicity of complex petroleum substances is controlled by the bioavailability of hydrocarbons, which can be predicted using a model that accounts for the partitioning of hydrocarbons into dissolved and particle phases.
toxicity testing of complex petroleum substance is best done using a combination of modeling and biomimetics.
